Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
The weekend's posts all point at the same week: NVDA earnings on Tuesday, and whether Jensen comes back. Prof supplies the headline — “BREAKING: Jensen Huang discusses coming back to Nvidia. Odds he returns as $NVDA CEO have doubled to 20%” — and the framing: “I think Earnings this week will tell you if Jensen comes back at some capacity or not. (If at all possible)” (his numbers, unverified). iain supplies the tape read, with charts for both big indexes: on SPY, “pinched between ATH AVWAP + April 8th AVWAP. A close beyond either should signal buyer/seller aggression. Could build a HL this week, but I'm leaning toward LLs if Friday's low breaks. Keep it simple, no touch for me while we're chopping inside the Nov. 5th kill candle.” On QQQ, his chart says it plainer: “failure to reclaim the 21ema + declining MAs, likely continued chop until a reclaim of the 21ema and/or flush of the 200day” — with “resistance gaps above = heavy supply” at 748.65 and “unfilled gaps below = downside targets”. And the bigger picture, from iain again: “The indexes look like they may be attempting to establish a HL, which would be encouraging. but the bigger picture remains messy... declining EMAs overhead, damaged weekly charts, limited constructive leadership. The market has to prove the character is changing!!” Remz stacks the week's catalysts in one post — “$NVDA earnings on deck. Uncertainty surrounding $NVDA leadership. $ANT IPO potentially draining market liquidity. Monthly OPEX week adding even more volatility. Crypto volatility across the” (quoted to the visible cutoff) — and then posts the two sharpest trade ideas of the window: the NBIS short (“You can be bullish on a company long term, but that doesn't mean you have to be bullish on the chart in front of you. And right now, this chart is anything but bullish.”) and the APP long flag. Enrich's week forecast is the joke version of the same calendar — “Monday: Market dies. Tuesday: $NVDA crushes earnings. Wednesday: Gap-up + FOMC minutes. Thursday: $ANT IPO + Jensen returns. Friday: Euphoria + Burry flips bullish” — and his Sunday outlook video adds the watches (RKLB, DELL, SNDK, U) and the recap (RKLB 350%, GOOGL ran 300% — his numbers, unverified). His baskets split the market in two: “Power + Buildout: $CRDO $NBIS $BE $COHR. Or Biotech: $ARKG $XBI.” The constructive camp is Venu's tight flags — SPOT, U, FROG and APP, “Emerging Stage 2 leaders showing RS & signs of institutional interest. Tight price action after strong advances is worth watching!” — plus Sean's PEG discipline: “we dont trade the gap up. We wait.” DiCarlo is the other constructive voice, on the two assets that have fallen furthest: “New Bitcoin Bull Cycle. This weekend was the buy. 71% of the time, BTC runs 150–300% in 18 months.” (his numbers, unverified) and “It's almost time $GLD $SLV”, with weekly smart-money-zone charts for both. Your process gives four genuine qualifiers with triggers above the close: APP (three traders, flag over 414.29), SPOT (flag over 627.66), U (flag over $55) and FROG (flag over 114.44) — plus GLD and SLV as zone tests (reclaim 377.92 and 51.41 first) and NBIS as the window's only short (under 109). The declines, not entries: NVDA at a new 52-week low into Tuesday's earnings, GOOGL 26.54% under its high, and BTC under every average with the group split on the bounce. The extended names: AAPL printed a new 52-week high at 356.27 with no pullback, U sits 21.65% above its 50-day EMA and FROG 18.96% above its — the flags are the entries there, not pullbacks. The discipline is in the framing: the indexes are chopping inside the Nov. 5 kill candle and QQQ is the weakest of the four, but the tightest-looking names are flagging under their highs — and Tuesday's NVDA print is the next test.

  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
